newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - RTZ-CRA sees strong demand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - RTZ-CRA sees strong demand.

text.p: Anglo-Australian mining giant RTZ-CRA said on Thursday it expected to benefit from strong metal and mineral demand growth in coming years.

It added it saw no major imbalances between demand and supply in 1997. "Whatever the short term fluctuation in market prices, we believe the group will be a beneficiary of the strong growth in demand for our products which is in prospect over the years ahead," RTZ chairman Robert Wilson said in a statement accompanying the group's 1996 results.

"Stocks of most metals are at relatively modest levels and, while production of many metals and minerals is set to grow during 1997, there is little to suggest that significant imbalances will result," he added.
Wilson said the outlook for the world economy in 1997 was for steady if unspectacular growth accompanied by low inflation and interest rates.
"Demand for most raw material should advance, assisted by the ending of destocking that suppressed buying during the previous two years," he said.
"Such conditions provide a healthy backdrop for RTZ-CRA's continuing programme of investment," Wilson said.
Adjusted earnings for the group fell 24 percent in 1996 to US$1.096 billion from $1.441 billion due to sharply lower metal prices, adverse exchange rates and problems with its U.S. copper smelter.
But Wilson said action was taken to solve the problems at the Kennecott smelter and added "substantial improvement will become evident during 1997."
The smelter problems were offset last year by gains elsewhere, making the total fall in 1996 adjusted earnings equivalent to the negative impact from metal prices and currencies, RTZ-CRA said.
Lower prices reduced earnings by $311 million, while adverse exchange rates cost the mining firm $38 million.
Prices for RTZ-CRA's main metals, copper and aluminium, fell 22 percent and 16 percent respectively in 1996.
RTZ-CRA said it would benefit in 1997 from the first full year of production at the Greens Creek silver, zinc and copper mine in the United States.
Expansion of the Tiwai Point aluminium smelter in New Zealand and increased operations at the huge Escondida copper mine in Chile would also have a positive impact.
This year would furthermore see initial production coming from the gold projects at Lihir in Papua New Guinea and Pipeline in the United States, RTZ-CRA said.
Engineering at the $700 million Lihir project was 99 percent complete by end 1996. Construction was 67 percent complete.
Annual output from Lihir is expected to average 600,000 ounces of gold for the first 15 years.

The $280 million Pipeline project produced its first gold earlier this month. It will treat 3.5 million ounces of recoverable reserves during its 10 year life to produce average 368,000 ounces of gold per year, RTZ-CRA said.
Completion of the expansion at the Grasberg mine in Indonesia is expected in mid-1998.
RTZ-CRA said it expected to receive permission by the end of March for a $470 million project at the Escondida mine to treat oxide ore and produce 125,000 tonnes of refined copper per year.
If all goes according to plan, the first copper cathode should be produced in September 1998.
The $750 million Boyne Island aluminium smelter expansion in Australia is on schedule and should boost capacity by 230,000 tonnes to 490,000 tonnes by the end of 1997, it said.
